She presented an arterial pressure of 148/80 mm Hg, heart rate of 124 bpm, and partial pressure of oxygen (PO2) of 64 mm Hg. Her blood gas analysis revealed a pH value of 7.4.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 46-year-old woman with femur fracture from an accident was initially assessed with neurological signs (GCS 4, positive Babinski, Kernig sign, neck stiffness), hypoxia (PO2 64 mm Hg), and local thigh bruising. Chest CT showed bilateral lung exudative lesions and pleural effusion, and brain MRI revealed diffuse embolic signals in multiple brain areas. Transthoracic echocardiography detected a patent foramen ovale (PFO) shunt. Lung imaging improved by day 14, and after supportive care and hormone therapy, she was discharged with dysphasia and a closed fracture. Laboratory tests were not reported. This temporal progression with clinical, radiologic, and echocardiographic evidence supports the diagnosis of fat embolism syndrome following femur fracture.
